name: Landmark Cars Ltd
title: Landmark Cars Ltd - 543714 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Landmark Cars Q1 FY27 pro forma revenue grew over 22% YoY to a record Q1, with PAT nearly doubling; EBITDA margin about 5.8%.
summary.overview: Management reported its best-ever Q1 on pro forma revenue from operations, up over 22% YoY in a seasonally soft quarter, with PAT nearly doubling. Management attributed roughly 19 percentage points of growth to volume and about 3 points to OEM price hikes. Management said it will judge the business on EBITDA, PAT and cash profit rather than gross profit, given the mix shift toward newer brands with different margin structures. Q&A covered EV aftersales economics, the ChargeZone charging partnership, workshop capacity (expressed in bays rather than outlet count), rental costs and cost efficiency. Management gave no numeric quantification for the ChargeZone revenue share or for FY28 profit targets.

roughly similar to last two years, per CFO

financial_highlights.value: almost INR60 crore in Q1 FY27
INR27 crore for the quarter; rental cost roughly INR25 crore; Ind AS lease impact about INR2 crore
about 0.95x last year as stated by CFO

financial_highlights.value: approx. INR79 lakh in Q1 FY27
financial_highlights.change: up from INR73 lakh in Q4 FY26

segments.name: New vehicle sales
segments.commentary: New vehicle sales margin trend cited by analyst at 1.7% in FY25, 2.0% in FY26 and 2.3% now; management said price hikes give a one-time benefit and demand above supply reduces freebies. Management expects a normalised ~1.5% EBITDA margin on pro forma new car sales in Q2-Q4 FY27 when asked.

segments.name: Aftersales
segments.commentary: Management said aftersales is growing at about 14-15% historically; EV aftersales revenue per vehicle is higher, with EV margins (ex-warranty) similar to the ~15% currently cited, and not expected to be lower. Share of aftersales from high-growth brands is 19% vs 38% of new car sales from those brands, per analyst.

segments.name: Outlets
segments.commentary: Total outlets about 141 (77 showrooms and 64 workshops per analyst's question). Management stopped classifying outlets as new a couple of quarters ago.

guidance_outlook: Management expects a more normalised and consistent demand trajectory through the later part of FY27, with no repeat of the GST-related disruption seen in Q2 FY26.
Management expects cost (employee and other expenses) as a percentage of revenue to fall further as revenue grows; no quantified target given, with a detailed number promised later.
Capex guided at around INR50 crore for the year; Q1 spend below proportionate share, with no commitment for the rest of the year.
Borrowing costs described as stable; surplus cash to be used to repay working capital loans.
Management said it is in talks with OEMs and possible takeover opportunities but will proceed on its own terms; no timeline given.
Asked about FY28 reaching FY23 peak profit levels, management declined to commit, citing macro uncertainty.
capex_capacity: Mumbai (Jogeshwari) workshop of about 50,000 sq ft inaugurated to serve Mercedes-Benz, BYD and Jeep; BYD and Jeep part due to be completed in the next few months.
New Mahindra workshop in Hyderabad to start operations soon; existing Hyderabad Mahindra capacity already exhausted, per management.
BYD outlets in Pune became operational in July 2026; two new BYD outlets opened about 7-10 days before the call.
MG network to reach 17 outlets with an LOI received for an additional Ahmedabad showroom.
Management said workshop capacity will be added in bays rather than workshop count, and smaller workshops will be consolidated into larger sites.
demand_pricing: Management said OEM price hikes (Mercedes-Benz and others) raise absolute gross profit per car, not percentage margin, since Landmark receives a percentage of the hike.
Price contributed roughly 3% of the 22-23% top-line growth; the remainder (about 19%) was volume, per management ballpark.
Mercedes-Benz sold 9,786 units in H1 CY2026, up 9% YoY; Mercedes-Benz plans over 40 new global models from 2027.
MG: new SUV launching in August expected to boost volumes; new Majestor deliveries began last quarter.

Mahindra: strong momentum with more launches to come; BYD: supply to improve through the rest of the year, hybrids later this FY; Kia: Syros EV orders healthy, new Sorento in September; Honda: City facelift, ZRV and Alpha 0 EV later this year.
Management argued that competition such as Audi's share push expands the luxury market (about 50,000 units) rather than cannibalises it.
Premium and mass segments grew faster than luxury in recent months per Aryaman Thakker.

qa_highlights.question: Will OEM price hikes improve Mercedes gross margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Thakker said price hikes raise absolute margin per car but not the percentage margin, as Landmark receives a percentage of the increase.

qa_highlights.question: Could Audi's share push pressure Mercedes sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new entrants expand the luxury market; the segment has hovered near 50,000 units and luxury penetration fell last year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the ChargeZone partnership add revenue, and at what economics?
qa_highlights.answer: ChargeZone runs about 16,000 charging points; Landmark onboards EV customers and earns a recurring revenue share with wallet credits for customers. Commercials were not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Q2 margin normalisation and Mercedes QoQ revenue decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q2-Q4 to be normalised, with an EBITDA margin around 1.5% on pro forma new car sales; Q1 is seasonally the weakest quarter and Mercedes grew strongly YoY.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EV aftersales margin versus ICE?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EV margins are similar to the ~15% currently seen and are not expected to be lower; warranty costs (such as batteries) were excluded from the analysis.

qa_highlights.question: Will rental costs and cash conversion change?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said lease amortisation was about INR19 crore, with lease plus interest about INR27 crore; full-year rental cost expected around INR100-110 crore including Ind AS adjustments. EBITDA-to-CFO conversion was about 0.95x last year and expected to be similar.

risks_watch: Gross margin pattern is being reframed toward EBITDA/PAT; management declined quarterly gross profit breakup by segment for now, so quarter-on-quarter comparability is harder to verify.

Mercedes-Benz growth is seasonal: Q1 is the weakest quarter and management says 40% of business falls in H1 and 60% in H2, so the Q2-Q4 normalisation (around 1.5% EBITDA margin on pro forma new car sales) needs tracking.
ChargeZone revenue-share economics were not disclosed; the partnership's contribution cannot be sized yet.

EV aftersales margin (about 15%, ex-warranty) is management's current view and excludes warranty costs such as battery replacement; management said it is not expected to be lower but is being cautious.
Workshop capacity is now reported in bays rather than workshop count, and smaller workshops are being consolidated, so outlet-level tracking becomes less direct.
Rental cost guidance of roughly INR100-110 crore for the year and EBITDA-to-CFO conversion near 0.95x; watch whether cash repays working capital loans and finance cost falls.
FY28 peak-profit question was not committed to; cost-to-revenue reduction target promised later without a number.
key_quotes: Our financial year '27 started on a strong note with pro forma revenue from operations growing at over 22% year-on-year to deliver our best ever Q 1 performance in a seasonally soft quarter.
We have found that th e EVs run much more on the road as compared to ICE vehicles due to its lower cost of r unning.
We are not saying that it is going to be higher over a period of time. We are trying t o say that it is not going to be lower.
I wish I could say this in a VUCA world that we are all living in. We are on a trajectory which is going to take us there.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, EV aftersales and cash generation, with strong, specific claims about growth and capacity. Notably cautious and evasive on forward numbers: declined to quantify ChargeZone commercials, FY28 profit targets, the cost-reduction path and the gross profit breakup, citing macro uncertainty or future disclosure.
